from.place: proof: descent of a derived stalk morphism and detection of its quasi-isomorphism on a principal affine neighbourhood

title: Detecting a quasi-isomorphism of perfect complexes on a neighbourhood
statement: For a chain map between strictly perfect complexes on an affine open, if its induced map on the stalk complex at a point is a quasi-isomorphism, then it is a quasi-isomorphism after restricting to some affine open containing the point and contained in the original open [def-pc-scheme] [def-pc-perfect-complex] [def-pc-module-stalk-functor].

proof.text: The open stalk functor preserves zero objects and carries each finite-free retraction to a retraction of a projective module, by openModuleStalk_free_projective. Thus its image of each strictly perfect complex is bounded above with projective terms. Mathlib CochainComplex.isKProjective_of_projective and CochainComplex.IsKProjective.quasiIso_iff give a homotopy equivalence whose forward map is the given stalk map of f.

Apply the existing source stalk chain-map lifting theorem to the inverse of that homotopy equivalence, with Q as source and P as target. This supplies an affine V and a chain map g on V in the canonical comparison coordinates. Define c to be that canonical termwise openModuleStalkRestrictionComparison. Naturality of c identifies the stalk of the restriction of f composed with g with c(P).hom composed with the stalk forward-inverse composite composed with c(P).inv. Similarly for the inverse-forward composite at Q. Compose each given homotopy with these comparison maps and simplify inverse isomorphism identities. The original hU binder stays unchanged but is unused.

Apply the inverse-homotopies spreading theorem to f, V and the lifted g with the two transported homotopies. It gives an affine W inside U and a chain map gW with the two inverse homotopies for the exact restriction of f. Assemble HomotopyEquiv with this forward map and gW; Mathlib HomotopyEquiv.quasiIso_hom supplies the requested quasi-isomorphism.
